Subject: EmberTech pilot: latency/throughput & deployment path

Alex — great demo today, thank you. Quick recap and proposed next steps from my side: 

- Key signals you shared: ~120 sustained req/s, P95 target ~150ms, short multi-hour bursts up to ~800 req/s during peak sales events.
- Privacy note: you mentioned stores customer PII and needs VPC connectivity for audit controls (SOC 2 in scope).
- Primary goal: roll out real-time suggestion endpoint with <=200ms P95 and predictable cost.

Recommended path (short):
1) Pilot on Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) in us-west to validate tail latency at expected QPS.
2) Configure prefix/KV caching for session reuse to reduce per-token cost.
3) Run a 2-week load profile including burst tests; follow with a capacity-sizing workshop to finalize commit.

Attachments: I attached a pilot-scope workbook and a draft SLA for your procurement team to review.

Next steps: can we lock in a 60-minute sizing workshop with your infra lead and our infra SEs next Wed (7/18) or Thu (7/19)? I can send a calendar invite.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mcole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Attachment stubs: pilot-scope.xlsx (workbook), redwood-sla.pdf (SLA draft)

From: Alex Liu <alex@embertech.com>

Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.pr@embertech.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EmberTech pilot: latency/throughput & deployment path

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Traffic: the 120 req/s is steady across our inference front; typical payloads are short (<= 60 tokens). Peak bursts happen roughly 2–3x/day for 30–90 minutes when marketing campaigns hit — we measured peaks close to 800 req/s.
- Latency SLA: Product is targeting 150ms P95 globally but we can accept regional targets for pilot (us-west first).
- Security: SOC 2 and our PCI counsel prefer VPC peering + customer-managed KMS for any production traffic. For pilot we can accept a dedicated-hosted arrangement if there is a clear plan to move to Private VPC within 60 days.
- Budget: we have a procurement guardrail—commits above $75k/year need director approval. If Dedicated sizing keeps us below that we can proceed quickly; if not, we'll need a justification memo.

Can you confirm the approximate committed GPU type and a back-of-envelope monthly cost for the Dedicated pilot (2-week run + one month of buffer)? Also, can you share what the fallback would be if dedicated capacity is constrained during spikes (e.g., hosted overflow)?

Alex
Alex Liu
VP Product, EmberTech
alex@embertech.com

Alex — thanks for the detail, very helpful. Short answers inline below and a proposed next step plan.

- GPU & cost: For the pilot we recommend an rtx-6000-style reserved pool (4 x A10g-equivalent slots in us-west) to meet your burst windows. Back-of-envelope: ~ $18k–$24k/month for the reserved pilot capacity depending on a 1 vs 3 month buffer (I attached a capacity estimate workbook). We'll refine after the workshop.
- Security & VPC: Pilot options are (a) Dedicated reserved with VPC peering + customer KMS (recommended) or (b) hosted Dedicated with strict routing and audit export for procurement to review. We can enable a Private VPC transition plan within 45–60 days post-pilot if you need that in writing.
- Fallbacks: Redwood supports overflow routing to our hosted fleet with model-variant throttling and graceful degradation policies. For spikes you can opt into pre-configured burst capacity (pay-as-you-go) or policy-based fallback to a quantized model to preserve latency.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Confirm workshop: Wed 7/18 10:30–11:30 PT with your infra lead + our SEs.
2) Procurement will want the SLA + sample SOC evidence — redwood-sla.pdf attached.
3) Post-workshop we deliver an updated capacity estimate and a pilot statement of work (SoW) for signatures.

If that sounds right I'll send calendar invites and loop in our solutions engineer (Rishi) for the sizing session.

Cheers —
Marissa
